Name: delaySampling
Requirement: The command link shall sample each round-trip delay uniformly from 6 to 10 s.
Rationale: The published round-trip range (source B). A uniform distribution is assumed.

Name: statusPeriod
Requirement: The rover shall send a status message every 60 s.
Rationale: Sets how quickly the planner learns the rover state; the 60 s is assumed.

Name: commandBeforeWaypoint
Requirement: The rover shall not start a new waypoint without a received command.
Rationale: The rover drives only on commands from the planner.

Name: earthBeforeWaypoint
Requirement: The rover shall not start a new waypoint while Earth is out of view.
Rationale: Commands need a direct-to-Earth link.

Name: commandResend
Requirement: The planner shall resend a command for which no acknowledgement has arrived within 15 s.
Rationale: A dropped command must not stall the trip. The timeout must exceed the 10 s maximum round trip, or every command would be resent; the spec's 10 s is raised to 15 s.
Basis: Split from REQ-C2; timeout raised from 10 s

Name: statusReplacement
Requirement: The rover shall not resend a dropped status message.
Rationale: Status is periodic, so the next scheduled message supersedes a lost one.

Name: dropAndResendLogging
Requirement: The system shall log every dropped and resent message.
Rationale: Drops and resends feed the reliability result (REQ-MVP1.4).

Name: commandAcknowledgement
Requirement: The rover shall send an acknowledgement through the command delay as soon as it receives a command.
Rationale: REQ-C2.3 needs an acknowledgement; the 60 s status message is too slow to serve as one.

Name: visibilityFromTerrain
Requirement: The environment model shall calculate Sun and Earth visibility for each cell from the terrain horizon and the ephemeris.
Rationale: Real terrain shadows are what make the comparison credible.
Basis: Reworded from 'calculated from terrain, not hand-painted'

Name: roadOnlyChangesFlags
Requirement: Turning the road off shall change only the road flags in the environment maps.
Rationale: The road must be the only difference between the runs.

Name: footprint
Requirement: The rover shall fit a 170 mm × 170 mm footprint, within ±2 mm.
Rationale: Matches VIPER's footprint at 1:10.

Name: wheelSize
Requirement: Each wheel shall be 50 mm in diameter and 20 mm wide, within ±2 mm.
Rationale: Matches VIPER's wheel size at 1:10.

Name: boxBody
Requirement: The rover shall have a box-shaped body.
Rationale: One of VIPER's defining visual features.
Basis: Split from REQ-H2 ('recognisable features' replaced by the list)

Name: cornerWheels
Requirement: The rover shall have a wheel at each corner.
Rationale: One of VIPER's defining visual features.

Name: sidePanels
Requirement: The rover shall have panels on its rear, left and right sides.
Rationale: Shows where VIPER's solar arrays sit.

Name: frontMast
Requirement: The rover shall have a mast at the front.
Rationale: One of VIPER's defining visual features.

Name: printable
Requirement: All structural parts shall print in PLA on a 180 mm × 180 mm bed without supports.
Rationale: Keeps the build possible on a small, common printer.
Basis: Reworded from REQ-H3 (escape clause removed; the CAD section names no exception)

Name: levelSpeed
Requirement: The rover shall hold a commanded speed of 2 cm/s on level ground, within ±10%.
Rationale: VIPER's 20 cm/s top speed at 1:10.

Name: slopeClimb
Requirement: The rover shall climb a 15° slope of the demo surface (the printed terrain map on a rigid board, decision D2).
Rationale: Matches the simulation's 15° slope limit.
Basis: Split from REQ-H5; 'chosen demo surface' named from D2

Name: turnOnSpot
Requirement: The rover shall turn 360° on the spot on the demo surface.
Rationale: Skid steering must work on the board to follow replayed routes.

Name: endurance
Requirement: Starting from freshly charged cells, the rover shall drive continuously for at least 2 hours.
Rationale: Covers a full demo session without changing cells.
Basis: Reworded from REQ-H6 (start condition added from CK-H5)

Name: wifiCommands
Requirement: The rover shall accept waypoint commands over Wi-Fi.
Rationale: Lets the laptop replay a stored route.

Name: wifiStatus
Requirement: The rover shall report its position, heading and battery voltage over Wi-Fi.
Rationale: The route player needs feedback to keep the rover on the route.

Name: safeStop
Requirement: The rover shall stop within 1 s after 1 s passes with no message received.
Rationale: Stops a runaway rover if the link drops. The route player must therefore send a message at least once a second while a route runs.
Basis: Reworded from REQ-H8 (timeout made explicit, matching the safe-stop design)

Name: cost
Requirement: Total parts cost shall stay under £300, including filament and delivery.
Rationale: Project budget.

Name: massLimit
Requirement: The rover's mass shall stay under 0.8 kg.
Rationale: The spec's motor torque margins assume this mass.
Basis: Reworded from REQ-H10 (reason moved to rationale)

Name: scaleModelCaveat
Requirement: Every display, sign or video shown with the rover shall state that it is a scale model driving a replayed route.
Rationale: Viewers must not mistake the prop for a working rover.

Name: noPerformanceClaims
Requirement: Every display, sign or video shown with the rover shall state that its speed, slip and energy use say nothing about VIPER or a lunar road.
Rationale: The tabletop rover's physics do not scale to the Moon.

Name: chargingSafety
Requirement: The rover shall provide no path for charging the cells while they are fitted.
Rationale: The rover has no charge control, so charging NiMH cells inside it would be a heat risk. Cells are charged in an external NiMH charger.

Name: terrainInterface
Requirement: The environment model shall receive terrain height, slope and wider horizon terrain as GeoTIFF on the LOLA polar stereographic grid, in metres.
Rationale: Defined interfaces let each model be built and tested separately.

Name: ephemerisInterface
Requirement: The environment model shall receive time and Sun and Earth azimuth and elevation in degrees, from SPICE kernels or a table.
Rationale: Defined interfaces let each model be built and tested separately. The format is a proposed default.

Name: environmentMapsInterface
Requirement: The environment model shall provide slope, lit flag, Earth flag and road flag by cell and time, as gridded arrays, to the planner, command link and rover.
Rationale: Defined interfaces let each model be built and tested separately. The format is a proposed default.

Name: commandInterface
Requirement: The planner shall send each command, with command ID, target x and y, heading and mode, as a JSON message to the rover through the command delay.
Rationale: Routing commands through the delay is what makes communication delay part of the comparison. The format is a proposed default.

Name: statusInterface
Requirement: The rover shall send each status, with time, x, y, heading, state of charge, mode and command status, as a JSON message to the planner through the command delay.
Rationale: The planner only knows the rover state that reaches it through the delay. The format is a proposed default.

Name: runLogInterface
Requirement: The planner and rover shall write the route, state, solar power, load, events and results to the display and log, as Parquet or CSV.
Rationale: The stored run set and the display both depend on this log. The format is a proposed default.

Name: scenarioInterface
Requirement: Every block shall read the road setting, preset, start, goal, start time, seed and parameters from one versioned YAML scenario file.
Rationale: One versioned file keeps every block on the same settings and makes runs repeatable. The format is a proposed default.

Name: offRoadMobility
Requirement: On off-road cells, the mobility model shall use the no-road speed made good and slip values.
Rationale: Off-road behaviour is the baseline the road is compared against.

Name: roadMobility
Requirement: On road cells, the mobility model shall use the active road preset's speed made good and slip values.
Rationale: The road's effect enters the simulation only through the preset values.

Name: slopeLimit
Requirement: The planner shall reject cells above the 15° slope limit.
Rationale: VIPER's published slope limit (sources B and C).

Name: headingOffsetLimit
Requirement: While driving, the rover's body heading shall stay within ±50° of its direction of travel.
Rationale: Allows the rover to turn its panels towards the Sun while driving; the 50° is assumed.

Name: sunlitHeading
Requirement: In sunlight, the rover shall choose the allowed heading with the most solar input.
Rationale: Maximises charging while driving.

Name: shadowHeading
Requirement: In shadow, the rover shall face its direction of travel.
Rationale: There is no solar input to gain by turning.

Name: roadComparison
Requirement: The system shall run the same VIPER-class rover trip on real lunar south polar terrain twice, once with the road off and once with the road on.
Rationale: This comparison is the purpose of the demo.

Name: reportedResults
Requirement: For each run, the system shall report arrival time, distance, energy used, minimum state of charge, time in shadow, waiting time, peak slip, and pass or fail.
Rationale: These are the outputs a viewer compares between the two runs.
Source: MVP spec, Purpose; Demo scenarios (reported results)

Name: riskAndReliability
Requirement: The system shall report risk for each run as the minimum state-of-charge margin above reserve, the peak slip and the time in shadow.
Rationale: The Purpose statement names risk but does not say how it is measured; this defines it from outputs the spec already lists.

Name: reliabilityMeasure
Requirement: The system shall report reliability for each run as the number of dropped messages and the number of resent commands.
Rationale: The Purpose statement names reliability but does not say how it is measured. Both counts are zero in the stored run set, which uses 0% packet drops.

Name: comparisonDifference
Requirement: For each comparison, the system shall report the road-on minus road-off difference of every reported result.
Rationale: The Purpose is to show the difference the road makes, not only each run's values.

Name: reportEitherWay
Requirement: Every presentation of the results shall report them whichever way they turn out, including when the road makes little difference.
Rationale: A demo that only shows favourable results would mislead.
Basis: Reworded from the Demo scenarios statement

Name: caveatSimplifiedModel
Requirement: Every shared result shall state that it comes from a simplified model using assumed rover loads, slip and road performance.
Rationale: Viewers must not read the results as predictions of real road performance.

Name: caveatAutonomy
Requirement: Every shared result shall state that VIPER is driven by a human team, while this demo plans automatically.
Rationale: The automatic planner is a simplification of how VIPER is really operated.

Name: assumedValuesConfigurable
Requirement: The system shall expose every value marked Assumed in this spec as a setting in the scenario file (IF-07).
Rationale: Assumed values are placeholders that must change as test data arrives.
Basis: Reworded from 'every assumed value shall be configurable'

Name: fixedScenario
Requirement: Both runs of a comparison shall use the same start, goal, start time and terrain map.
Rationale: The road must be the only difference between the runs.
Basis: Reworded from 'each comparison shall use one fixed start, goal, start time and terrain map'

Name: widerTerrainForShadows
Requirement: The shadow calculation shall include a lower-resolution terrain map extending beyond the 2 km patch, with its extent to be decided.
Rationale: Distant ridges cast shadows into the patch. The wider map is still an open decision.
Basis: Reworded from the Environment conditions statement

Name: demoSite
Requirement: The demo shall use the Connecting Ridge site, or Connecting Ridge Extension if no patch at Connecting Ridge passes the selection rules.
Rationale: It combines strong published illumination with an image-enhanced terrain model.
Basis: Split from the site selection statements; fallback added from the spec's prose

Name: patchSelectionRules
Requirement: The 2 km patch and scenario date shall be chosen by applying the spec's site selection rules in order.
Rationale: Fixed rules make the choice of patch traceable rather than cherry-picked. This is a requirement on how the scenario is set up.
Basis: Split from the site selection statements

Name: r2Framing
Requirement: Every presentation of scenario R2 shall describe it as selected to illustrate the problem, not as a typical trip.
Rationale: R2 is chosen because a shadow matters, so it is not representative.
Basis: Reworded from the Demo scenarios statement

Name: precomputedRunSet
Requirement: The system shall precompute and store a run for every viewer control combination: 3 no-road and 9 road runs per scenario, 24 in total.
Rationale: The viewer can then change controls without replanning, in any product form.
Basis: Reworded from the run set statement

Name: displayIndependence
Requirement: The system shall generate and store the run set without the final display installed.
Rationale: The product form is not yet decided.
Basis: Reworded from 'shall stay independent of the final display' ('usable' made testable)

Name: repeatableRuns
Requirement: Given the same scenario file and random seed, the system shall produce identical run results.
Rationale: Repeatable runs let reviewers reproduce any result and confirm that only the road changed.

Name: failureConditions
Requirement: The system shall mark a run as failed when charge falls below reserve, the rover enters a cell above the slope limit, or the rover has not arrived by the end of the scenario.
Rationale: Pass or fail is a reported result, so its conditions must be defined.
Basis: New ID for a spec statement

Name: solarReferenceCase
Requirement: With the Sun at 0° elevation facing a rear corner, the power model shall give 450 W of solar input, within 5%.
Rationale: Sets a pass tolerance and condition for the spec's 'about 450 W'.

Name: drainReferenceCase
Requirement: With a constant 600 W load and no solar input, the power model shall take a full battery to empty in 9.0 h, within 5%.
Rationale: Sets a pass tolerance and condition for the spec's 'about 9 h' (5,420 Wh at 600 W).

Name: shadowCredibility
Requirement: At least 80% of the shadow-edge speeds sampled along both runs' routes during the scenario shall fall within the published 0.1 to 1.8 cm/s.
Rationale: Sets a pass threshold for the spec's 'most shadow-edge speeds'.

Name: chargeBounds
Requirement: The power model shall keep state of charge between 0 and 1.
Rationale: Charge outside this range has no physical meaning.

Name: excessSolarDiscarded
Requirement: The power model shall discard solar power that a full battery cannot accept.
Rationale: Stops a full battery being credited with energy it cannot store.

Name: timeAndEnergy
Requirement: For each route it evaluates, the planner shall calculate travel time and energy from the active speed, slip and load.
Rationale: Time and energy are what the road changes.

Name: reserveLimit
Requirement: The planner shall not plan driving that takes state of charge below the battery reserve.
Rationale: Falling below reserve fails the run (REQ-MVP12).
Basis: Split from REQ-R2; the slope limit part is REQ-M2

Name: earthLimit
Requirement: The planner shall not plan driving while Earth is out of view.
Rationale: Driving needs a direct-to-Earth link.

Name: routeCost
Requirement: Among the routes it evaluates, the planner shall choose the one with the lowest cost, where cost is arrival time plus 0.001 h per Wh drawn from the battery.
Rationale: A stated cost function can be checked; 'minimise' alone cannot. The energy penalty is assumed.

Name: planTime
Requirement: The planner shall finish each plan within 5 min of wall-clock time.
Rationale: Matches the 5 min command cycle; the value is assumed.

Name: fullResolutionRecheck
Requirement: The planner shall recheck the final route at full terrain resolution.
Rationale: A coarse-grid plan could miss a steep or shadowed cell.
